notes: Observations, not failures. (1) The harness lives in orchestration/evidence/tmp-T1.5/ (git-ignored). (2) claims check applies the test-once rule per claimed run, so a claim on the earliest test record still passes when a later un-overridden test record exists; check_run flags the later record. This follows the plan's wording (same function, applied to the claimed record). (3) A retrieval-only record that saves grounded_rate or unsupported_claim_rate as None triggers the judge requirement, because recompute_metrics emits those keys as None for rows without cards. A writer that omits None-valued metrics is unaffected. (4) The 'must also fail when' rule for timestamps and run_id versus filename is not enforced (records are found by glob on experiment name), so a hand-forged record outside the E#-*Z.json pattern would not be seen. Writers use write_run, which names files correctly. (5) I did not read earlier tasks' tests for weakening beyond confirming the full suite passes (194).
